title: Cyrus and the Asset
premise: August Nystrom, a traumatized interpreter for a collapsing peace delegation, discovers her own voiceprint buried in a foreign intelligence server—proof that someone weaponized a recording of her testimony from 'the incident' to sabotage the talks. Pursued by both the agency that betrayed her and the faction that wants the secret silenced, she allies with Cyrus Vane, a disgraced fixer whose loyalty she can never fully verify. As the delegation's final session approaches, August must decide whether to trade the recording—the one thing that could expose the truth and clear her conscience—for Cyrus's life. She chooses justice over safety, releasing the file publicly at the cost of her anonymity, and the two escape into new identities, together but forever changed.
about_author: Petra Dunmore is a former diplomatic translator who spent a decade in negotiation rooms across three continents before turning to fiction. She writes thrillers about the people history forgets: the interpreters, couriers, and witnesses standing just outside the frame.

chapters.title: The Language of Insomnia
chapters.summary: August Nystrom, POV. Three months after 'the incident,' August interprets for a fractious peace delegation in Geneva, running on four hours of sleep and careful routines. A near-miss with a delegate's aide rattles her; she realizes someone is watching her. Emotional beat: brittle control masking dread.

chapters.title: Dead Air
chapters.summary: August, POV. Reviewing archived audio for the delegation's records, August hears her own voice—a phrase she never said aloud in any official room—embedded in a corrupted transmission file. The metadata points to a server in Tallinn. Emotional beat: vertigo; the past is not where she left it.

chapters.title: Cyrus
chapters.summary: Cyrus Vane, POV. Introduced in a rain-slicked Riga safehouse, Cyrus is a former intelligence fixer now selling discretion to the highest bidder. He's hired to retrieve the same corrupted file—and finds August's name already flagged on three watchlists. Emotional beat: professional curiosity curdling into unease.

chapters.title: Voiceprint
chapters.summary: August, POV. Using a journalist contact's equipment, August confirms the voiceprint matches her exactly: someone cloned her testimony from the incident to fabricate evidence that sank the peace process. Before she can copy the file, the server wipes itself remotely. Emotional beat: cold clarity—she was never a witness, she was ammunition.

chapters.title: The Handler's Smile
chapters.summary: August, POV. Her nominal protector within the delegation, Deputy Chief Marion Kessler, gently suggests August take leave. August recognizes the maneuver: they want her isolated before the final session. She pretends to comply while booking a flight under a false name. Emotional beat: betrayal sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Two Thieves
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. Cyrus intercepts August at the Riga airport—not to stop her, but because his client's instructions have changed from retrieve to eliminate, and he doesn't kill people he hasn't met. He offers an uneasy alliance: he knows who owns the server. Emotional beat: wary transactional trust.

chapters.title: What the Incident Was
chapters.summary: August, POV. On a night train to Warsaw, August finally tells Cyrus the truth: she mistranslated—or refused to translate—one sentence that would have triggered a massacre, and the real recording of that moment vanished. Someone has been holding it over her ever since. Emotional beat: confession as relief and exposure.

chapters.title: Kessler's Ledger
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. Cyrus breaks into a delegation annex and finds Kessler's private ledger: payments routed through the same shell company that owns the Tallinn server. Kessler isn't protecting the talks; she's being paid to guarantee their failure. Emotional beat: grim vindication.

chapters.title: Safehouse Arithmetic
chapters.summary: August, POV. Hiding in a Kraków safehouse, August and Cyrus work out the timeline: whoever holds the original incident recording can destroy or exonerate her at will. The final delegation session is nine days away. An attempt on the safehouse forces them to move early. Emotional beat: intimacy forged under pressure.

chapters.title: The Man Who Buys Silence
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. In Vienna, Cyrus meets his former employer, Aldous Rehm, ostensibly to close out the contract. Rehm reveals he has the original recording—and that he'll trade it for the fabricated file's last surviving fragment, which August copied without knowing. Emotional beat: the trap closing softly.

chapters.title: Terms of Trade
chapters.summary: August, POV. August learns what Cyrus concealed: that his original contract targeted her. The fight between them is quiet and devastating. She agrees to the trade anyway—but only if the recording goes public, not into Rehm's vault. Emotional beat: love against duty, first fracture.

chapters.title: Nine Hours in Bratislava
chapters.summary: August, POV. The handoff is set in a riverfront hotel. August rehearses her role while noticing surveillance that doesn't match Rehm's people—a third party is in play. She copies the fragment again, hiding it where no one would think to look: inside a translation exercise file. Emotional beat: cunning rekindled.

chapters.title: The Third Party
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. Cyrus identifies the watchers: a faction within the delegation's security detail who want both recordings destroyed and every loose end—including Kessler—removed. He warns Rehm, who dismisses him. Cyrus realizes Rehm plans to double-cross everyone. Emotional beat: loyalty shifting from employer to August.

chapters.title: Kessler Runs
chapters.summary: August, POV. Kessler, sensing the net tightening, contacts August secretly: she'll testify about the payments if August gets her out. It's either redemption or bait. Against Cyrus's advice, August agrees to meet her. Emotional beat: mercy as calculated risk.

chapters.title: Ambush on the Danube
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. The meeting becomes a trap set by the security faction. Kessler is killed; August and Cyrus barely escape across the river, and Cyrus takes a bullet through the shoulder. August drags him to a clinic run by an old colleague. Emotional beat: guilt, fury, and the cost of trust.

chapters.title: What August Decided
chapters.summary: August, POV. While Cyrus recovers, August stops waiting. She reconstructs the full chain—fabricated voiceprint, Kessler's ledger, Rehm's ownership—and prepares to release everything at the delegation's final session, using the venue's live broadcast as an unkillable channel. Emotional beat: fear transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: Rehm's Offer
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. Rehm makes a final offer: the original recording, unedited, in exchange for August walking away permanently. Cyrus stalls, buying hours, knowing Rehm intends to kill them both regardless. He sends August a coded warning hidden in a phrase only an interpreter would catch. Emotional beat: devotion expressed in tradecraft.

chapters.title: The Final Session
chapters.summary: August, POV. August infiltrates the conference center as contracted interpretation staff. As the closing statements begin, she patches the archive into the broadcast feed. The fabricated voiceprint plays, then the authentic incident recording—her refusal, and the truth of who ordered the massacre. Emotional beat: the climax; her voice, finally hers.

chapters.title: Collapse
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. Chaos erupts: delegates walk out, Rehm's men storm the control room, and Cyrus holds the corridor long enough for the upload to complete and propagate to mirrors worldwide. Rehm is arrested by the very security faction he'd outbid, trading accusations as they take him. Emotional beat: sacrifice vindicated.

chapters.title: Aftermath in Grey Light
chapters.summary: August, POV. Hearings begin; August testifies anonymously, her identity protected by the scandal's sheer size. She reads the coverage in a Vienna café and feels the insomnia loosen for the first time in months. Justice came outside the law, and it cost everything except herself. Emotional beat: exhausted peace.

chapters.title: New Names, Old Promise
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. Cyrus burns his remaining contracts and meets August at a coastal town under names neither will keep forever. He offers no explanations, only the choice to stay or go. She stays—at least until the next train. Emotional beat: guarded tenderness.

chapters.title: The Interpreter Sleeps
chapters.summary: August, POV. Epilogue. Months later, August teaches translation to refugees, anonymous and unremarkable. One night she sleeps through till morning and wakes to sunlight and Cyrus making coffee badly. Somewhere, the recording still circulates, keeping the truth alive. Emotional beat: quiet resolution—love chosen over survival, freely.
